items.title: Airbag 0x57 never answers (PIWIS address, fast init)
items.notes: RESOLVED & ISOLATED 2026-10-28: Car-tested on Pin-3-isolated line. Kombi 0x64 (28ms) and Climate 0x98 (74ms) woke instantly, proving Pin 3 to VS 90 is 100% intact. Airbag ECU (Temic MRSZ 996.618.219) confirmed powered, grounded, and functional via 60s 1Hz tell-tale deactivation flash (WSM 69-D26). Exhaustive testing (fast init 20-100ms, 5-baud 0x57/15/08/01/33, 9600 baud, 256-addr sweep, and 80s continuous poll across deactivation window) returned 0 bytes. Root cause isolated strictly to physical layer: open circuit on Pin 9 (0.35 OR/BL) between VS 90 and M563 connector, or blown K-line transceiver IC on Temic PCB. Full field log: field_logs/2026-10-28_airbag_diagnostic_investigation_and_pin3_isolation.md; review pack: docs/reports/frontier_review_airbag_0x57_investigation_2026-10-28.md.

items.notes: 2026-10-18 session (406 passes, field_logs/2026-10-18_kombi_backup_fuel_adapt_and_engine_off_session.md): FUN_04de32 @ 0x84DE32 proves OBD Mode 01 LTFT1/2 is literally 0x380AAA/0x380AA9 (FRA1/2 >> 8). Once warm (t>340s), FRA1/2 adapted upward from 0.861/0.848 (-14.1%/-15.6%) to 0.952/0.948 (-4.8%/-5.2%), settling at 0.939/0.931 (-6.25%/-7.03%), while during the 3-min warm stationary idle RKAT1/2 (0x3838EE/0x3838EC) climbed from +2.48%/+2.67% to hit a ceiling at +4.5000% (0x0060) on both banks! Decision: LTFT stays ~0 with in-spec pressure -> the negative bias was an adaptation artifact, no longer a live issue; re-adapts toward ~-10 % with in-spec pressure -> real (MAF over-read / O2 / purge). items.notes: Owner feature request expanded 2026-10-19 / 2026-10-20: Unified speedometer calibration assistant across platforms. 1) Presets: a) 'OEM Factory Buffer (+10%)' = DEFAULT baseline, preserving factory UNECE R39 behaviour; b) 'Raw Sensor Wheel Speed (~+3.5% to +4% over GPS)' = (RECOMMENDED) matching 1:1 what ABS/DME/Kombi see on the wire, naturally legally compliant without software markup; c) '100% True GPS Speed' = GATED behind an interactive in-car GPS logging & steady-speed capture calibration wizard before writing (ensuring true vehicle-specific rolling radius is sampled); d) 'Custom Profile' = freeform input for user %/mph offset and non-stock tyre size calculator (recalculating K-Zahl 21 70 / 3B 70 and Tacho_Kennlinie 21 78 00 / 3B 78 00 w1..w4). CRITICAL MULTI-POINT CURVE MATH: Tacho_Kennlinie_1X (10 bytes = 5 little-endian 16-bit words [w0, w1, w2, w3, w4]). Breakpoints: w0=0, w1=12.25 km/h (7.6 mph), w2=116.39 km/h (72.3 mph), w3=283.00 km/h (175.8 mph), w4=390.50 km/h (242.6 mph). Urban/commute speeds (0-72 mph) are interpolated strictly between w1 and w2; w3 only affects >72 mph. Any calibration factor R MUST scale ALL FOUR non-zero words (w1, w2, w3, w4) uniformly (w_i_new = round(w_i_base * R)) to preserve exact dial linearity without flat spots or kinks. For UK 180 mph dial (base uk2: 00 00 C9 04 77 2D 8C 6E 8A 98): Raw Wheel Speed preset uses R=1.0605 (00 00 13 05 37 30 3B 75 C2 A1); True GPS Speed preset uses R=1.0976 (00 00 41 05 E7 31 55 79 6C A7).

items.title: Modular diagnostic stack: layered architecture (hardware → transport → protocol → application) with standard library reuse
items.notes: ARCHITECTURE REVIEW + IMPLEMENTATION PLAN. Goal: make the diagnostic stack modular, expandable, easy to understand, KISS. Reuse good existing libraries; do not reinvent. Current state: bespoke K-Line code in tools/kline_probe.py + helper/openpiwis_helper/ handles KWP2000 (ISO 14230) over serial, ISO 9141 5-baud init, OBD-II modes, and Porsche-specific services (0x10, 0x12, 0x14, 0x17, 0x18, 0x19, 0x21, 0x22, 0x23, 0x27, 0x3E, 0x2E, 0x30, 0x31, 0x32). No CAN/UDS support yet (987/997 parked). Target architecture: 4 layers. LAYER 1 - HARDWARE (extract): K-Line serial (FTDI/D2XX/pyserial) from gkbus KLineHardware + bespoke FTDI/D2XX glue. CAN bus from python-can (industry standard, BSD-3, many backends: SocketCAN, PCAN, Kvaser, Vector). LAYER 2 - TRANSPORT (extract): K-Line (ISO 9141) from KWP2000-CAN kline.py. ISO-TP (ISO 15765-2) from python-can-isotp (MIT, mature, well-tested). TP20 (VAG) from KWP2000-CAN can.py. LAYER 3 - PROTOCOL (extract + bespoke): KWP2000 (ISO 14230) from gkbus kwp2000.py + KWP2000-CAN. UDS (ISO 14229) from udsoncan (MIT, extensive docs, active community) or py-uds (MIT, multi-bus, client+server, error injection). OBD-II from python-obd (BSD-3, ELM327) + bespoke K-line OBD. LAYER 4 - APPLICATION (bespoke, per-generation): Porsche-specific services. 986/996 (K-Line): DTC read/clear (0x14, 0x17, 0x18 with groupOfDTC), freeze frames (0x12), ECU ident (0x1A), memory read (0x23), coding (0x22, 0x2E), actuator tests (0x30, 0x31, 0x32), security access (0x27), TesterPresent (0x3E). 987/997 (CAN/UDS): same services via UDS 0x10, 0x19, 0x1A, 0x22, 0x23, 0x3E + KWP2000 over CAN (TP20) for pre-UDS modules. 981/718 (CAN/UDS): same stack, different ECU addresses + service sets. PHASE 1 (986/996 K-Line, improve existing): Extract hardware abstraction from gkbus. Extract KWP2000 command/response pattern from gkbus. Extract SecurityAccess (0x27) implementation from gkbus. Keep bespoke K-Line timing + Porsche-specific services. Add OBD-II command tables from python-obd. PHASE 2 (987/997 CAN/UDS, new head start): Add python-can as CAN transport. Add python-can-isotp as ISO-TP transport. Add udsoncan (or py-uds) as UDS application layer. Extract KWP2000 over CAN (TP20) from KWP2000-CAN. Write Porsche-specific application layer (ECU addresses from WP12, service sets, coding, actuator tests). Enforce read-only allow-list (AGENTS.md rule 1). PHASE 3 (981/718, future): Reuse same CAN/UDS stack. Add 981/718-specific ECU address tables + service sets. Transport layer shared across all generations. KEY PRINCIPLES: KISS - reuse good existing code, do not reinvent. Layering - each layer depends only on the one below. Expandable - adding a new generation = new application layer, same transport/protocol. Easy to understand - clean separation, standard library names, minimal bespoke code. Libraries researched 2026-10-28: KWP2000-CAN (EliasTuning, MIT, KWP2000 over CAN+K-Line, TP20, DS2, 6 stars, Dec 2025), gkbus (KWP2000 over CAN+K-Line, CCP, SecurityAccess, v0.4.90, Oct 2026), openobd (Jifeline, commercial, ISO 14230 K-line, TP2.0, DoIP, OBD, v1.26.11, Sep 2026), python-obd (BSD-3, OBD-II, ELM327, <1.0.0), py-uds (MIT, UDS multi-bus, client+server, error injection, Python 3.12+, K-Line planned), python-can-isotp (MIT, ISO-TP, python-can integration, v2.x, 199 commits), python-can (BSD-3, CAN bus, industry standard), udsoncan (MIT, UDS, CAN, extensive docs, active community). Deliverables: (1) Architecture document in docs/specs/ describing the 4-layer design with library choices + rationale. (2) Refactored helper/openpiwis_helper/ with clean layer separation. (3) New CAN/UDS transport + protocol modules for 987/997. (4) Updated tools/kline_probe.py to use the new layered stack. (5) Tests for each layer. (6) Updated AGENTS.md + README.md with the new architecture. (7) Updated docs/features.yaml + docs/STATUS.md. Acceptance: python tools/run_all_tests.py passes. 986/996 K-Line still works (replay tests pass). 987/997 CAN/UDS stack is in place and ready for first car contact. Architecture is documented and easy to understand. No bespoke code where a standard library already exists.
